transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Please tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... I guess what brought me in is that... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but some nights after work, or maybe if I've had a tense dinner, I start eating and... it's like the decision-making part of me just sort of shuts off? Like I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but I just can't seem to make myself stop. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly, or like I just need better willpower, and I'm sure you deal with much more serious things, but... does that make sense? Is that the right kind of thing to talk about here?
When you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah, exactly. Um, like I was just mentioning a second ago, it really does feel like I just can't make myself stop. 

I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm totally unhinged or anything—I'm actually a very responsible person normally! I manage everything fine at work and all that. But just in those specific moments... yeah, it's like my brain knows I should stop, and I want to, but my hands just keep reaching for more and the decision-making part of me is just offline. 

Is that... is that something you hear from other people? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Do these episodes bother you or interfere with your life in any way, like making you feel ashamed, affecting your relationships, or impacting your daily routine?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say it's ruining my life or anything dramatic like that. I mean, I still show up for all my shifts at the store—I'm a cashier, by the way—and I handle all my responsibilities just fine. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart! 

But... I guess it does bother me a little bit. Sometimes, after an episode, I... well, I might skip out on a family dinner, or if I do go, I'm kind of distracted. I just get so caught up worrying about what I ate, or... or figuring out what I need to do afterward to sort of fix it, if that makes sense? 

I feel terrible when I'm not fully present with my family, and I know I should just push past it. Does that sound like the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
After these eating episodes, do you ever do anything to try to 'undo' or compensate for what you ate, like making yourself sick, exercising a lot more than usual, or skipping meals?

Um... yeah. Yes, I do. I mean, I really hope you don't judge me for this, because I know it's not the healthiest way to handle things, and I feel really awful even saying it out loud. 

But... yeah, for the last few months, it's been happening most weeks. I'll have one of those nights where I just lose control, and then... I just feel so guilty, you know? Like I have to fix it somehow. So, um, sometimes I'll make myself throw up, or I might take some laxatives. Other times I'll just skip meals the next day, or force myself to go on a really, really long walk to try and burn it off. 

I know it sounds terrible, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I just... I get so anxious about gaining weight or letting myself go. Is that... does that make sense why I would do that? I hope I'm not shocking you or anything.
Do these eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling down, stressed, or anxious, or do they seem to happen more randomly, without a clear trigger?

Um... you know, I haven't really noticed a clear pattern like that. I hope that's an okay answer, I just... I don't want to give you the wrong information. 

I mean, I get stressed sometimes, sure—just normal everyday stuff at work, nothing I can't handle! But these eating things... they kind of just seem to happen randomly? Like, I could be having a perfectly fine, normal Tuesday, and then suddenly I'm just in the middle of it. 

I guess I haven't really been paying close enough attention to what my mood is right before it starts. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not very helpful for your notes. Do you... do you want me to start keeping track of that? I can absolutely start writing it down if it would make your job easier. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative use, and excessive exercise, along with concerns about body weight and shape, aligns with the diagnostic criteria for bulimia nervosa (F50.2). There is insufficient evidence for anorexia nervosa (F50.0) as there is no report of significant weight loss or fear of weight gain leading to restrictive eating. The specificity of the symptoms reported makes F50.81 (other specified eating disorder) less likely, narrowing the diagnosis to F50.2.
